title: The Arab and His Camel
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 骆驼得寸进尺，最后把主人挤出了帐篷。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: AS AN Arab sat in his tent one cold night, he saw the curtain gently lifted, and the face of his Camel looking in.
paragraphs.zh: 一个寒冷的夜晚，一个阿拉伯人坐在帐篷里，看见帘子被轻轻掀起，他的骆驼探进头来。

paragraphs.en: “It is cold, master,” said the Camel; “suffer me, I pray thee, to hold my head within the tent.”
paragraphs.zh: “主人，天太冷了，”骆驼说，“求您让我把头伸进帐篷里吧。”

paragraphs.en: “By all means,” replied the hospitable Arab; and the Camel stood with his head inside the tent.
paragraphs.zh: “当然可以，”好客的阿拉伯人回答；于是骆驼把头伸进了帐篷。

paragraphs.en: “Might I also warm my neck a little?” he entreated after a moment.
paragraphs.zh: “我能不能再把脖子也暖和一下？”过了一会儿，他恳求道。

paragraphs.en: The Arab readily consented, and the Camel’s neck was thrust within the tent.
paragraphs.zh: 阿拉伯人爽快地答应了，骆驼的脖子也伸进了帐篷。

paragraphs.en: He stood, moving his head from side to side uneasily, and presently said: “It is awkward standing thus. It would take but little more room if I were to place my forelegs inside the tent.”
paragraphs.zh: 他站在那里，不安地左右晃着头，不久说道：“这样站着真别扭。要是我把前腿也放进帐篷，也占不了多大地方。”

paragraphs.en: “You may place your forelegs within the tent,” said the Arab. And now he had to move a little to make room, for the tent was small.
paragraphs.zh: “你可以把前腿放进帐篷。”阿拉伯人说。这时他不得不挪一挪，腾出地方，因为帐篷很小。

paragraphs.en: The Camel spoke again: “I keep the tent open by standing thus, and make it cold for us both. May I not stand wholly within?”
paragraphs.zh: 骆驼又说：“我这样站着，总把帐篷口敞着，害得我们俩都冷。我能不能整个儿站进来？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” said the Arab, whose compassion included his beast as well as himself; “come in wholly if you wish.” But now the tent proved to be too small to hold both.
paragraphs.zh: “可以，”阿拉伯人说，他的怜悯既给了自己，也给了自己的牲口，“你想进来就整个儿进来吧。”可这时帐篷已经小得容不下他们两个了。

paragraphs.en: “I think, after all,” said the Camel, as he crowded himself in, “that there will not be room here for us both. You are the smaller; it will be best for you to stand outside. There will be room then for me.” So he pushed a little, and the Arab with all haste went outside the tent.
paragraphs.zh: “我想，说到底，”骆驼一边往里挤，一边说，“这里容不下我们两个。你个子小些，最好你站到外面去。这样就有地方给我了。”于是他稍稍一推，阿拉伯人只好赶紧站到了帐篷外面。
